## Source: Current standalone qualification

Canonical source: [docs/qualification-0.2.1.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/qualification-0.2.1.md)

# Standalone performance and reliability

This qualification measures the bounded-port standalone implementation in
v0.2.1. It is separate from the [original UDP comparison](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).
Every receipt identifies its executable and source; no result establishes
maximum WAN capacity or full coturn compatibility.

The [build and source receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/qualification-builds-0.2.1.json)
matches both ordinary native release executables to the binaries measured
in the primary matrices. PGO and portable alternatives are explicitly
separate experiments.

## Complete M4 matrix

The [full native M4 matrix](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-final-0.2.1.json) completed 108
runs and 53,075,648 measured forwarded packets without observed payload
loss, reordering or corruption. Three repetitions cover 1/16/128 allocations,
160/1,200-byte payloads and both servers over UDP/TCP/TLS. Like the Linux
matrix, it uses an eight-packet window per load worker. At least 200,000
round trips and two seconds are required in each throughput phase.

| Client transport | spry packets/s at 128 allocations / 1,200 B | coturn packets/s | Difference at that cell | Difference across all six cells |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 271,644 | 223,168 | +21.7% | +16.2% to +22.2% |
| TCP | 302,240 | 305,790 | -1.2% | -1.2% to +8.5% |
| TLS | 264,697 | 196,161 | +34.9% | +27.1% to +34.9% |

Values are medians of three runs. This is an Apple M4 Max with 16 logical
CPUs, native ARM64 executables and existing workloads left running. Rust
1.96 builds use generic ARM64, LTO, one codegen unit and stripped symbols.
The default connected-UDP feature and optional TLS are enabled; no PGO or
M4-only instructions are used for these primary results. Coturn 4.18.0 is
the pinned, unmodified reference with database backends and Prometheus
disabled, `-O3 -DNDEBUG` and `relay-threads=0`.

The two complete matrices contain 216 runs and 96,423,584 checked packets.
Their payload checks passed; the separate Linux kernel counters still have
their own scope. These rates and three-run medians do not establish a
maximum capacity, statistical significance or a result for every machine.

## Controlled M4 tuning

Three repetitions, 128 allocations, 1,200-byte payloads, four native load
workers and a 32-packet window per worker. Each throughput phase runs for
at least two seconds and completes at least 200,000 round trips. Server
order alternates, with fresh processes and credentials. Both servers use
the same bounded UDP relay-port range. All executables are native ARM64;
the Rust server includes optional TLS in every row.

| Client transport | v0.2.0 packets/s | v0.2.1 packets/s | coturn packets/s | v0.2.1 against coturn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 291,196 | 292,464 | 244,760 | +19.5% |
| TCP | 312,708 | 330,799 | 340,869 | -3.0% |
| TLS | 273,799 | 285,779 | 213,236 | +34.0% |

These are medians of delivered forwarding rates in the
[27-run controlled experiment](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-tuning-0.2.1.json). No loss,
reordering or payload corruption was observed in completed runs. The UDP
peer leg remains UDP with every client transport. TLS negotiated TLS 1.3
and AES-256-GCM-SHA384 for both servers; the load client validates the
generated localhost certificate through an explicit test trust store.

The retained runtime change caches each stream's writable-interest state.
The event loop registers writable readiness when output becomes blocked,
then removes it after draining. It avoids a registration syscall for every
packet while keeping read interest active. No dependency, thread, unsafe
block or packet buffer was added. A real-socket unit test forces
backpressure, drains the queue, checks the transition back to read interest
and verifies later forwarding. The controlled medians improve spry-turn's
own TCP throughput by 5.8% and TLS throughput by 4.4%.

| Client transport | spry loaded RTT p99, µs | coturn loaded RTT p99, µs | spry process RSS, MB | coturn process RSS, MB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 836.7 | 1,006.3 | 2.24 | 11.35 |
| TCP | 778.5 | 1,010.4 | 12.21 | 11.70 |
| TLS | 872.2 | 1,273.6 | 14.89 | 20.43 |

Loaded RTT includes time queued behind the batch, both relay directions,
client work and the echo peer. It samples every 64th packet into bounded
per-worker reservoirs. The separately recorded sequential RTT is measured
before throughput; its small changes do not support a general latency-win
claim. Stream buffers cost memory: spry-turn's TCP RSS exceeds the tested
coturn configuration here. Decimal MB excludes kernel memory and shared
dependency files.

## Linux ARM64 virtual machine

The [complete Linux matrix](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-final-0.2.1.json) contains 108
successful runs: three repetitions across 1/16/128 allocations, 160/1,200
byte payloads, UDP/TCP/TLS and both servers. It completed 43,347,936 measured
forwarded packets with no observed payload loss, reordering or corruption.
This is native ARM64 Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit inside Docker on Apple M1, with
a two-vCPU quota, 2 GiB container memory limit and approximately 4 GiB
VM-visible RAM. Existing host/VM workloads remained running; this is not
bare-metal Linux or an otherwise idle machine.

Both servers use the same eight-packet window on Linux. Initial 32-packet
bursts exceeded coturn's default 32 KiB TCP output congestion threshold:
26 × 1,204-byte frames passed, while 28 frames exceeded that bound. Coturn
intentionally drops peer datagrams under that pressure. The initial trial
did not complete; its surviving UDP timings also use that different window.
Those results are retained as [Linux diagnostics](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-burst-failure-0.2.1.json)
alongside the complete matrix. A later M4 PGO experiment using the same
32-packet window also encountered coturn congestion; its
[partial receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-burst-failure-0.2.1.json) is excluded from
the primary and PGO comparison figures.

| Client transport, 128 allocations / 1,200 B | spry packets/s | coturn packets/s | spry loaded RTT p99, ms | coturn loaded RTT p99, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 56,511 | 66,823 | 11.073 | 5.712 |
| TCP | 151,614 | 103,278 | 2.167 | 4.085 |
| TLS | 54,424 | 41,801 | 7.510 | 8.541 |

The M4 advantage does not generalise to every Linux case. UDP is slower in
five of six Linux matrix cells. At the row above, spry-turn trails coturn
by 15.4% over UDP and leads by 46.8% over TCP and 30.2% over TLS. These are
workload medians on this constrained VM, not a general platform ranking.

At that allocation/payload size, spry/coturn process RSS medians are
2.286/11.682 MB for UDP, 6.484/11.882 MB for TCP and 8.991/16.945 MB for
TLS. The raw receipt separately records process-owned socket counters.
Some TCP/TLS socket drop counters are nonzero even though every measured
payload arrived correctly; TCP recovery and kernel counters have a
different scope from the generator's payload checks. Do not report this
as zero kernel drops or total system-memory use.

## Reproduce and interpret resources

Build the load generator with the same TLS feature and native target as
the server. Supply unmodified coturn built by the pinned preparation script.

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --features tls \
  --target aarch64-apple-darwin --bin spry-turn --example load
python3 scripts/prepare-coturn.py .local/reference
python3 scripts/compare.py \
  --spry target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/spry-turn \
  --loader target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/examples/load \
  --coturn .local/reference/coturn-4.18.0/bin/turnserver \
  --required-arch arm64 --runs 3 --clients 1 16 128 --sizes 160 1200 \
  --transports udp tcp tls --packets 200000 --min-seconds 2 \
  --output .local/qualification.json
```

Use `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` on native ARM64 Linux, or the actual native
target on another host. The runner refuses architecture mismatches when
`--required-arch` is supplied. `--baseline` adds a reviewed alternative
server, `--workers` controls generator concurrency and
`--coturn-relay-threads` records the reference configuration. These are
benchmark controls, not worker support in the server.

For the Linux matrix, supply `--window 8` and use
`python3 scripts/prepare-coturn.py .local/reference --prefix /usr` with the
distribution's libevent/OpenSSL development packages installed.

This is a closed-loop delivered-packet workload. More allocations do not
mean every allocation is independently saturated. Duration floors improve
sampling but do not establish maximum sustainable packets/s. CPU seconds
cover server startup, allocation setup, warm-up, both measurement phases
and resource inspection. Duration-floor runs can deliver different packet
counts, so total CPU alone cannot establish efficiency. The generator runs
in a separate process and is excluded from server CPU accounting.

RSS is sampled every 50 ms. Descriptor and socket-memory snapshots are
taken after throughput while all client connections and allocations remain
live, before releasing the generator. They are quiescent snapshots, not
peak socket memory. Linux attributes `ss -m -e` records to process-owned
socket inodes and aggregates each counter separately. In particular,
`rb`/`tb` are configured ceilings, not allocated memory. The counters do
not include every kernel object and must not be added to RSS to claim
total system memory. macOS reports this measurement as unavailable;
the extra connected UDP socket per allocation still needs a descriptor
and kernel-memory budget. See the [Linux ss manual](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html).

## Application and remaining acceptance

The actual [KithMoot web application](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md) has a separate
generated-media runner. It enters operator credentials through the real
Connections settings and checks that the client makes no `/turn` request.
Browser certificate bypass is explicitly distinct from the trusted test
TLS used by the native benchmark client.

Private cross-network operation, trusted public certificate lifecycle,
physical GrapheneOS calls, long-lived refresh/credential renewal and
independent security review remain separate gates. Archy and Sapflow
integration follow standalone qualification; no publisher-operated service
is added by this work.

---

## Source: KithMoot acceptance

Canonical source: [docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md)

# KithMoot client acceptance

spry-turn speaks standard TURN. KithMoot can use that transport without
adding KithMoot, WebRTC or media codecs to the server. Each device chooses
its operator and enters the credentials supplied for that relay. The
publisher need not run a relay or credential service.

## Run the actual web application locally

The acceptance runner builds an authorised KithMoot source checkout using
its existing Node dependencies, then serves that unchanged production app
on loopback. It starts a disposable Nostr signalling fixture and a separate
spry-turn process. Each browser enters the operator's short-lived TURN
credentials through the real Settings → Connections form. The shared
secret stays in the fixture; only its expiring username and credential
reach the client. The fixture refuses `/turn`, and the test asserts that
the application never requests it. No credential service is needed.

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --features tls --bin spry-turn
python3 tests/kithmoot.py \
  --kithmoot /path/to/authorised/kithmoot \
  --binary target/release/spry-turn \
  --output .local/kithmoot-web.json
```

Install KithMoot's pinned dependencies in that checkout beforehand. The
runner uses this repository's Playwright installation and Chromium, as
described in [standalone verification](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/verification.md). `--app-dist`
accepts an existing production build instead; its content digest is
recorded, and the receipt says whether the runner built it. No source from
the other project is committed into this repository. The receipt identifies
the source commit, relevant file checksums, app build digest and exact
spry-turn executable hash.

For each transport, two independent browser contexts create and join a
real KithMoot room, then use its camera and microphone controls. The
application's own “Hide my IP address” preference selects relay-only ICE.
The test observes peer connections and rejects any direct configuration;
it supplies no substitute ICE servers. Both sides must display remote
video, decode video frames and receive audio bytes with positive audio
energy. Selected candidates must be relay candidates at both ends with
the requested relay protocol. HTTP and signalling are restricted to local
fixtures; generated camera frames and an oscillator are the only media.

The default run qualifies UDP, plain TCP and TLS separately in Chromium.
KithMoot's explicit device relay path preserves plain TCP where the browser
supports it. WebKit rejects that URI and needs UDP or TLS alternatives;
this Chromium run does not qualify WebKit. The app's legacy same-origin
credential resolver has different filtering rules and is not the path
tested here. spry-turn's independent
[socket and browser suites](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) also cover all three server
transports. The invitation is checked to exclude the device's username and
credential.

The runner stops its servers and browser processes, including on failure,
and removes its temporary build and credentials. The requested JSON
receipt contains counters and digests, without room invitations, TURN
credentials, addresses or machine paths. Keep raw failure logs private:
browser error messages can include a room invitation.

## What this proves

This is real web application and server interoperability on one machine.
It exercises KithMoot's explicit relay Settings, room signalling, media
controls, peer negotiation and decoded media through spry-turn. Browser
TLS uses an explicit test-certificate bypass. It establishes neither
trusted public certificate validation nor cross-network reachability.

spry-turn does not add an HTTP credential issuer, a publisher-operated
service or a hosted default. The operator generates short-lived credentials
locally and distributes those to their clients. This fixture qualifies the
identified web source and executable, rather than every released KithMoot
client or an unrelated public deployment.

## Choose an operator on each device

The KithMoot web source at
[`24038110`](https://github.com/forgesworn/kithmoot/commit/24038110cd4a60037b5e3f6a6c0131af65478102)
provides Relay addresses, Relay username and Relay password under
Settings → Connections. Enter the TURN URLs alongside the credential
minted for that operator, then leave and reopen the room. The device
choice takes precedence over the room's ICE URL hints. Credentials remain
on the device and are omitted from invitations. Never put the shared TURN
secret into a client, room link or descriptor.

The older room ICE field carries URLs alone; it is insufficient to provide
a TURN username and password. Use the explicit call-relay Settings rather
than treating that field as a credential mechanism.

Android source at
[`c0ad53b2`](https://github.com/forgesworn/kithmoot-android/commit/c0ad53b20fa3ed50900bf672916d3aa458634c05)
also has explicit per-device `CallRelayConfig`, with credentials associated
only with the saved URLs. Its relay-only resolver returns no relay when
none is configured. That source inspection is separate from executing a
native call against spry-turn; no Android binary was changed or tested by
this runner.

Existing coturn accounts using persistent usernames and passwords cannot
be reused unchanged: spry-turn currently supports shared-secret REST
credentials. Keep a working private coturn instance until clients have
chosen and accepted a separate spry-turn instance with its own credentials.

Expiring credentials need operator renewal. These device Settings do not
establish an automatic renewal service. Qualify the standing-call,
credential replacement and reconnect behaviour before relying on long
sessions. Room membership and identities remain separate from transport
credential issuance.

## Independent deployment and GrapheneOS gate

Before replacing an existing TURN deployment, test a separately chosen
operator with the [firewall, NAT and certificate plan](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md).
Use two different access networks and trusted certificates. Force each
client transport in turn, confirm the actual selected relay pair and
bidirectional displayed media, then repeat with client UDP blocked.
Keep relay-to-peer UDP available: TURN over TLS does not change that leg.

On a physical GrapheneOS device without sandboxed Google Play, configure
the operator in the actual native client. Verify native/web media in both
directions, network changes, a standing call
through allocation and credential renewal, reconnect and explicit expiry
failure. Check that unavailable credentials never silently defeat a
relay-only choice. Record the installed package identity, selected
transport and sanitised counters independently from browser evidence.

No Android device was attached during this source inspection. The existing
native browser interoperability instrumentation is emulator-only; do not
run it on a person's physical phone. Native compilation, emulator checks
and physical GrapheneOS acceptance are distinct gates, and none is supplied
by this web runner. Archy installation follows standalone acceptance.

---

## Source: Performance experiments

Canonical source: [docs/performance-experiments.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/performance-experiments.md)

# Performance experiments

These experiments inform later runtime changes. The shipping server keeps
its existing dependencies, one event loop and ordinary release build.

## Linux UDP receive batching

The separate development crate in `experiments/linux-batch` measures a
specific question: how much receive-call overhead can be amortised when
several UDP datagrams are already queued on one descriptor? It adds no
dependency or feature to the spry-turn runtime.

It uses pinned nix 0.31.3 with only `net` and `uio` features. Its safe
[`recvmmsg` API](https://docs.rs/nix/0.31.3/nix/sys/socket/fn.recvmmsg.html)
and preallocated `MultiHeaders` avoid introducing unsafe code here. The
call uses `MSG_DONTWAIT` and no kernel timeout: the documented Linux
timeout behaviour can otherwise leave a partly filled call blocked.

Run on Linux from the repository root, sharing the existing target tree:

```sh
cargo fmt --manifest-path experiments/linux-batch/Cargo.toml -- --check
cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path experiments/linux-batch/Cargo.toml \
  --target-dir target --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --manifest-path experiments/linux-batch/Cargo.toml \
  --target-dir target
cargo build --locked --release \
  --manifest-path experiments/linux-batch/Cargo.toml --target-dir target
target/release/spry-linux-batch-experiment --packets 65536 --runs 3 \
  > .local/linux-batch.jsonl
```

Every variant first queues the same 32-datagram offered window, then drains
it. A single `recv_from` baseline is compared with `recvmmsg` capacities
1, 8 and 32. Payloads are 160 and 1,200 bytes. One hot receiver socket is
contrasted with 32 receiver sockets holding one ready datagram each. These
are unconnected sockets; this does not measure spry-turn's connected-UDP
path. Order
rotates between repetitions. Warm-up traffic is excluded from reported
packet counts and timing. All sockets bind loopback on ephemeral ports;
there are no services, files containing credentials or fixture threads.
Each sample has a wall-time bound and stops on an unexpected receive result.

The receiver timer includes source, sequence and every payload-byte check,
but excludes sending and queue fill. Whole-workload time includes those
sender costs. Output is newline-delimited JSON: a method record followed
by raw samples. Receive-call counts are instrumented API calls, not an
independent `strace` measurement. Returned batch occupancy, payload arena,
I/O-view and header storage are reported. Header storage follows the pinned
dependency's structures and excludes allocator overhead. Socket receive
buffer limits are configuration values, **not measured kernel memory**.
Whole-process RSS and forwarding latency are not supplied by this tool.

This is a receive-queue microbenchmark, not maximum network throughput or a
spry-turn performance result. It deliberately arranges ready queues. Real
TURN allocations spread traffic across sockets; increasing batch capacity
cannot combine packets from different descriptors. Extra arena space and
header setup may cost more than the saved calls when queues hold only one
packet. Any integration must demonstrate an improvement in the actual
server, including fairness, p99 latency, full supported datagram sizes and
kernel memory, before changing the runtime.

### Recorded run

The coordinated Linux VM run completed all 48 samples: 3,145,728 measured
datagrams, with no observed source, ordering, length or payload failures.
The [receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-batch-0.2.1.json) and
[raw newline-delimited samples](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-batch-0.2.1.jsonl) retain the
method, build identities and results.
The two focused tests also passed. The binary was built with Rust 1.94.1
for aarch64, using a two-vCPU container quota and a 2 GiB container memory
limit inside the configured 4 GiB VM. This is distinct from native M4 or
bare-metal Linux forwarding measurements.

The table shows median whole-workload cost reduction against `recv_from`,
including the sender. Positive values mean less elapsed time; negative
values mean more. Receiver-only timings and every raw sample are retained
in the experiment receipt.

| Ready receiver sockets | Payload | Batch 8 cost reduction | Batch 32 cost reduction | Packets per batch call, 8 / 32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| One hot socket | 160 B | 7.5% | -16.0% | 8 / 32 |
| One hot socket | 1,200 B | 17.7% | 23.6% | 8 / 32 |
| 32 sockets, one queued packet each | 160 B | -26.7% | -29.7% | 1 / 1 |
| 32 sockets, one queued packet each | 1,200 B | 14.0% | -30.6% | 1 / 1 |

Batch 8 reduced receiver-plus-validation time by 27–37% for one hot
socket. Larger capacity did not provide a consistent whole-workload gain.
With a single packet per socket, batch 32 still required one receive call
per packet and increased whole-workload cost by about 30%. Three runs in a
shared VM include scheduling noise; the mixed cells must remain visible.

The 1,200-byte receive arena grows from 1,200 bytes for the baseline to
9,600 bytes for batch 8 and 38,400 bytes for batch 32. The corresponding
preallocated header structures add 696 and 2,616 bytes, excluding allocator
overhead. Actual server support for full UDP datagrams would need a larger
arena or another deliberate buffer strategy.

The experiment remains outside the runtime. It identifies queue occupancy
as a requirement for a useful batching path; it does not establish that
spry-turn should batch every allocation or that the server became faster.

## Default and portable builds on Linux

The portable trial compares two builds of the **same 0.2.1 runtime and
loader source**, alongside unmodified coturn. Both spry builds include TLS
and the stream-interest optimisation. The default build also enables
`connected-udp` and `direct-index`; the portable build enables only
`runtime,turn,tls`. The receipt calls the portable variant `spry-baseline`
because that is the comparison script's optional second-binary label.
It is not the historical 0.2.0 source baseline.

The [build identities](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-variants-0.2.1.json) record identical
release settings, generic aarch64 targets and unset `RUSTFLAGS`. Both
executables are 1,381,008 bytes. The original default executable and loader
were copied and hash-verified before rebuilding in the same target tree.

The [27 socket runs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-portable-0.2.1.json) completed
10,830,224 forwarded packets without an observed payload error. Each run
uses 128 allocations, four load workers, 1,200-byte payloads and an
8-packet window per worker. The throughput phase completes at least
200,000 round trips and lasts at least two seconds. Fresh server order
alternates across three repetitions per transport and variant.

These measurements ran in a two-vCPU, 2 GiB container inside a configured
4 GiB Docker Desktop LinuxKit VM. Existing physical-host workloads remained
running. This is a constrained VM observation, not isolated Linux hardware
performance. The ranges below retain the substantial variation between
repetitions; all rates are delivered forwarded packets per second.

| Client transport | Default median (range) | Portable median (range) | coturn median (range) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 86,149 (68,986–121,028) | 67,539 (53,104–87,014) | 84,155 (83,311–212,893) |
| TCP | 127,926 (100,460–137,656) | 91,631 (77,892–96,418) | 103,053 (72,228–103,106) |
| TLS | 54,373 (39,376–82,748) | 45,436 (44,015–73,021) | 42,366 (31,027–47,489) |

All three medians favour the default in this trial. The wide ranges and
shared VM do not establish that feature selection caused those differences.
There is no measured case here for changing the shipped runtime to the
portable variant.

The descriptor trade-off is concrete. At 128 UDP allocations, the default
holds 257 UDP sockets and 262 descriptors, against 129 sockets and
134 descriptors for the portable build. Median process RSS is about
2.732 MB and 2.740 MB respectively. Quiescent Linux `ss` counter `f`
reports 1,052,672 and 528,384 bytes; it is one socket-memory accounting
field, not total kernel memory. The corresponding summed `rb` buffer
ceilings are about 54.9 MB and 27.6 MB: these are configured limits, not
resident allocations. TCP/TLS allocation socket counts are the same in
both builds. Neither the similar RSS nor these individual counters prove
equal total system memory.

To reproduce, preserve the first build before selecting portable features.
Use the checkout's existing target tree and a locally prepared coturn
reference as described in [the main comparison](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md#reproduce).

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu \
  --features tls --bin spry-turn --example load
mkdir -p .local/variants
cp target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/spry-turn .local/variants/spry-default
cp target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/examples/load .local/variants/load
cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu \
  --no-default-features --features runtime,turn,tls --bin spry-turn
cp target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/spry-turn .local/variants/spry-portable
python3 scripts/compare.py \
  --spry .local/variants/spry-default --baseline .local/variants/spry-portable \
  --loader .local/variants/load \
  --coturn .local/reference/coturn-4.18.0/bin/turnserver \
  --required-arch arm64 --runs 3 --clients 128 --sizes 1200 \
  --transports udp tcp tls --window 8 --min-seconds 2 --packets 200000 \
  --output .local/linux-portable.json
```

## Independent process scaling

The [worker experiment receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/linux-workers-0.2.1.json) compares
one and two independently addressed default spry-turn processes, then
repeats the same comparison with coturn. It adds no worker feature to the
server. The total workload remains 128 allocations and four load workers:
two processes receive 64 allocations and two workers each, with disjoint
relay-port ranges. Both servers use one relay event loop per process.

A readiness barrier releases the generators after all server probes pass.
Each generator then performs its own allocation setup, warm-up and
sequential latency sampling. Throughput phases are therefore not perfectly
aligned. The tool estimates each phase end from the arrival of its flushed
result line and subtracts the generator's reported duration for its start.
Aggregate rate divides all delivered packets by the enclosing interval
across those phases. It does not sum the individual process rates. Pipe
and scheduling delays introduce timing uncertainty; the receipt records
each estimated interval and its overlap.

Twelve groups, comprising 18 server-process runs, completed 6,422,416
forwarded packets without an observed payload error. The workload uses
UDP, 1,200-byte payloads and window 8, with three repetitions of each
server/process-count case. Each process receives its share of 200,000
minimum round trips and runs its throughput
phase for at least three seconds. The VM and container limits are the same
as the portable trial above.

| Server | Processes | Estimated aggregate median packets/s | Range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| spry-turn | 1 | 137,795 | 129,886–138,317 |
| spry-turn | 2 | 167,677 | 140,077–257,081 |
| coturn | 1 | 94,876 | 88,071–178,757 |
| coturn | 2 | 270,221 | 135,910–275,201 |

Two-process phase overlap is 92.8–99.7% for spry-turn and 80.8–98.9% for
coturn. These variable VM samples do not establish linear scaling or a
stable comparative advantage. Separately addressed processes also need
explicit client distribution; this experiment supplies no shared listener,
automatic failover or maximum-capacity result.

For spry-turn, the median sum of individual post-phase process RSS
snapshots grows from 2.736 MB to 5.329 MB. Descriptor counts grow from
262 to 268 and UDP sockets from 257 to 258. Those snapshots are not a
simultaneous whole-system peak. The summed `f` socket-memory counter grows
from 1,052,672 to 1,056,768 bytes; other kernel allocation structures remain
outside that counter. Complete server CPU time is 1.929 s and 2.381 s,
including startup and resource inspection. The duration floor produces
different delivered packet counts, so these CPU totals alone do not measure
CPU efficiency at equal work.

Use the preserved default executable and loader from the build commands
above. The [script](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/scripts/worker-scaling.py) refuses to overwrite an
existing evidence file and stops its own server and generator processes
on completion or failure.

```sh
python3 scripts/worker-scaling.py \
  --spry .local/variants/spry-default --loader .local/variants/load \
  --coturn .local/reference/coturn-4.18.0/bin/turnserver \
  --required-arch arm64 --processes 1 2 --runs 3 \
  --clients 128 --workers 4 --packets 200000 \
  --size 1200 --window 8 --min-seconds 3 \
  --output .local/linux-workers.json
```

## Profile-guided optimisation

The [M4 PGO comparison](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-pgo-0.2.1.json) uses the same source,
release settings and TLS feature as the ordinary build. Only the profile
compiler flags differ. A finite Rust embedding host trains the actual
server library with generated UDP/TCP/TLS traffic at both payload sizes,
then exits normally so LLVM can write its counters. Training covers six
workloads with 16 allocations. The profile is checked for nonzero execution
counters before use.

The 27-run comparison uses 128 allocations, 1,200-byte payloads, window 8,
three repetitions and the same duration/count floors as the main runner.
All runs passed payload checks. The receipt's `spry-turn` label means the
experimental PGO build; `spry-baseline` is the ordinary v0.2.1 release build.

| Client transport | Ordinary release packets/s | PGO packets/s | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| UDP | 282,300 | 286,885 | +1.6% |
| TCP | 315,054 | 317,897 | +0.9% |
| TLS | 270,745 | 273,211 | +0.9% |

Those small median changes are within the scale of run variation; the
experiment does not establish a worthwhile general throughput gain. The
executable shrinks from 1,197,760 to 1,181,520 bytes. The shipping artefact
remains the ordinary release build, which does not depend on a workload
profile or a particular training machine. A different representative
workload or larger repeated study could justify revisiting that choice.

The [training receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/pgo-training-0.2.1.json) and
[build/profile identity](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/qualification-builds-0.2.1.json) identify
the training host, loader, merged profile and compiler settings.
The first continuous-profile attempt produced files whose counters were
all zero. They were rejected, and no rates based on that profile are used
here. The finite host produced six raw files with a merged total count of
166,916,851 and maximum function count of 14,045,496. Compiler warnings
for unexercised functions are retained locally; this training is not full
path coverage or correctness qualification. A 32-packet-window attempt
also encountered coturn congestion; its partial receipt is linked from
the [main qualification](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/qualification-0.2.1.md#linux-arm64-virtual-machine).

Follow the [Rust PGO workflow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/profile-guided-optimization.html)
with the matching toolchain's `llvm-profdata`. Use a fresh private profile
directory and the checkout's existing target tree. Preserve the ordinary
server and loader before instrumentation, as in the portable experiment.
For example, on native Apple ARM64:

```sh
rustup component add llvm-tools-preview
mkdir .local/pgo
SPRY_PGO_DIR="$(pwd)/.local/pgo"
SPRY_LLVM_PROFDATA="$(rustc --print target-libdir)/../bin/llvm-profdata"
RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate=$SPRY_PGO_DIR" \
  cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
  --features tls --example profile_server
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$SPRY_PGO_DIR/%p.profraw" \
  python3 scripts/train-pgo.py \
  --server target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/examples/profile_server \
  --loader .local/variants/load --profile-dir "$SPRY_PGO_DIR" \
  --profdata-tool "$SPRY_LLVM_PROFDATA" --output .local/pgo-training.json
RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-use=$SPRY_PGO_DIR/merged.profdata -Cllvm-args=-pgo-warn-missing-function" \
  cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
  --features tls --bin spry-turn
```

All other compiler flags must match between instrumentation and profile
use; keep any path-remapping flags in both stages. The finite host is
restricted to loopback and generated test credentials. Profiles and raw
logs remain private scratch. Compare the resulting binary against the
preserved ordinary build with the same native loader; it is still a
closed-loop workload rather than maximum network capacity.

## Source: Verification

Canonical source: [docs/verification.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/verification.md)

# Standalone verification

## v0.2.1 qualification

The stream-readiness optimisation passed ten all-feature Rust unit tests,
including actual TCP backpressure, queue draining, removal of writable
interest and subsequent progress. Twenty-seven independent socket tests
passed on macOS and native ARM64 Linux, including the five added malformed
input, integrity and expiry regressions. A later
[fixture startup correction](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/fixture-startup-0.2.1.json) adds five
independent subprocess regressions, giving **32 passing tests** on both
platforms. It reserves TCP/UDP together, keeps TLS separate and bounds
collision retries, startup reads and cleanup. The unchanged public API remains
at the v0.2.0 configuration shape.

On Apple M1, the [180-second churn run](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/stress-0.2.1.json) completed
30,137 allocations, 3,767 signed port-exhaustion responses and 337 refreshes
of a short-lived standing allocation. It exercised UDP/TCP/TLS, failed
authentication, private-peer rejection and resumed forwarding. Server
descriptors returned from nine to nine; process RSS rose from 2.08 to
4.19 MB. Its fixed regression budget and duration are not a leak proof.
The same receipt records seeded datagram loss, delay and reordering,
credential expiry/replacement, partial-stream reclamation, TCP/TLS paused
reader recovery and post-overload progress.

The [300-second ASan/libFuzzer campaign](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/fuzz-0.2.1.json) completed
15,241,706 inputs with zero crash artefacts, `cov=698` and `ft=1561`.
It records the target/core hashes, seed, toolchain and corpus digests.
This is coverage-guided codec/auth testing, not network-runtime fuzzing or
independent security acceptance.

The [hardened wrapper smoke run](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/fuzz-wrapper-0.2.1.json) adds a
separate 30 seconds and 344,105 inputs after lockfile preflight and process
cleanup changes. It also passed with zero crash artefacts. The earlier
300-second receipt retains the exact wrapper and parser hashes it tested.

The [actual KithMoot web application](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/kithmoot-web-0.2.1.json),
source `24038110`, passed generated bidirectional decoded video and audio
through spry-turn over UDP, TCP and TLS. Both browsers configured owner
credentials through Settings, selected relay candidates, omitted credentials
from invitations and made zero `/turn` requests. See the
[reproduction and limits](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md). Browser TLS bypasses its
test certificate; the native benchmark client separately validates a
generated certificate through its test trust store.

The [current comparison](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/qualification-0.2.1.md) contains complete M4 and
Linux matrices: 216 runs and 96,423,584 checked packets, plus a controlled
v0.2.0/v0.2.1/coturn tuning trial over all three client transports. It supersedes no
historical receipt: each identifies its own method and source. Public
firewall/NAT, trusted public certificate renewal, physical GrapheneOS and
Archy acceptance remain open. The existing independently operated private
coturn deployment was inspected read-only and remains unchanged.

## Bounded relay ports, local increment

The optional UDP relay-port range passed 22 independent socket tests with
the default TLS build, including a signed 508 on exhaustion, occupied-port
skipping, reuse after deallocation and continued forwarding by another
allocation. Chromium passed relay-only generated audio/video/data over
UDP, TCP and TLS, with selected local and remote relay ports asserted
inside the configured range. See the [bounded receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/bounded-relay-ports-20261023.json).
The existing initial-release benchmark and hosted CI below do not qualify
this new runtime change. Public firewall/NAT, certificate lifecycle, Archy
installation and phone acceptance remain unverified.

## Initial implementation evidence

23 October 2026. Private MIT software project; no public relay, credential
endpoint, application service or Archy integration has been deployed.

- Rust fmt and all-feature clippy passed with warnings denied.
- Eight all-feature unit tests passed, including the published STUN vector,
  tampering, parsing bounds, nonce binding/expiry, rate accounting, private
  peer policy and stale-event isolation with bounded slot reuse.
- Minimal builds passed: one limits test without features; six codec/auth
  tests without the socket runtime.
- All 19 independent socket tests passed with the TLS build, including UDP,
  TCP, TLS, framing, credentials, quotas, expiry, permissions, indications,
  channel traffic and isolation across deallocation/reallocation.
- Chromium passed relay-only data round trips, decoded generated video and
  received audio at both endpoints over UDP, TCP and TLS. No real camera,
  microphone recording or production room was used. Browser TLS tests use
  explicit test-certificate bypass; the independent Python TLS client
  validates the generated certificate through its test CA.
- Actual WASM execution validated the STUN integrity vector and a million
  arena framing/parsing operations without linear-memory growth. Its timing
  is a protocol microbenchmark, not a network performance measurement.
- The final native ARM64 M4 comparison completed all 36 runs, 14.4 million
  forwarded packets, with no observed data loss, reordering or corruption.
  See [method, trade-offs and raw evidence](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).
- The staged source/credential scan passed without an ignore rule. Recorded
  checksum fields use explicit path/SHA-256 records; no test credentials,
  private endpoints, machine paths or actual media are committed.

At the initial verification, GitHub hosting was private under
`forgesworn/spry-turn`. Publication to package
registries, image registries, public releases and Pages remains disabled or
absent. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/actions/runs/40015270709)
passed on Linux and macOS for implementation commit
`48d75adf51c73b1ef2a51a3cb663e424f2b4ea35`. That run predates the bounded-port
increment; hosted CI is separate evidence from the new local checks.

Retained local build evidence is ignored by Git:

- `.local/bin/spry-turn`: tested native executable with optional TLS enabled.
- `.local/wasm/`: generated WASM module and JavaScript/TypeScript bindings.
- `.local/evidence/m4-benchmark-source.tar.gz`: exact M4 benchmark source
  snapshot, identified by the committed build receipt. Rustfmt normalisation
  matches the reviewed Rust files. Repository ownership metadata subsequently
  changed to the ForgeSworn organisation without changing runtime source.

Task-owned test servers and browsers have stopped. The M4 scratch tree was
removed after evidence capture, and `cargo clean` removed 340.2 MiB of local
build output. Existing unrelated host services are preserved. Real-phone,
lossy-network, Linux performance, full coturn conformance and public operator
acceptance remain the explicit later gates in [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md).

## Source: Acceptance and roadmap

Canonical source: [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md)

# Compatibility and acceptance

## First standalone implementation

- [x] Original Rust STUN/TURN parser with published integrity test vector.
- [x] Real UDP allocations and bidirectional relaying.
- [x] Coturn-compatible shared-secret REST credentials, signed responses,
  stateless address-bound nonces and expiry.
- [x] UDP, TCP and optional TLS client transports, with bounded stream buffers.
- [x] Permissions, ChannelBind, indications, refresh/delete and allocation retry.
- [x] Local Chromium relay-only data and decoded media over UDP/TCP/TLS.
- [x] M4 comparison against unmodified coturn, with method and raw results.
- [x] Native connected-UDP and direct-readiness-slot tuning, tested against
  a native baseline and coturn with resource costs recorded.
- [x] WASM protocol arena, actual execution and bounded buffer reuse test.
- [x] Public MIT source, source/secret review and CI readback.
- [x] Controlled bounded-port M4 UDP/TCP/TLS comparison against v0.2.0 and
  coturn, with a measured stream-readiness optimisation.
- [x] Actual KithMoot web application: device-selected credentials, relay-only
  generated media over UDP/TCP/TLS and no credential-service request.
- [x] Bounded local allocation churn, injected loss/jitter, credential expiry,
  slow-client recovery and 300 seconds of coverage-guided ASan fuzzing.

## Before replacing an existing deployment

- [x] Operator-selected bounded UDP relay port range and firewall/certificate plan.
- [ ] Applied firewall/NAT, trusted public certificate lifecycle and independent
  cross-network deployment acceptance; a local plan is not this evidence.
- [ ] Cross-network KithMoot web and physical native interoperability against
  a separately chosen operator, without a project-operated credential service.
- [ ] Packet-loss, jitter, blocked UDP, IPv6, long-lived refresh, reconnect,
  certificate validation/renewal and resource-exhaustion qualification.
- [ ] Broader RFC conformance and longer network/runtime fuzzing campaigns;
  the recorded bounded codec/auth campaign is not a security review.
- [ ] Independent security review, including nonce/auth state and relay targets.
- [ ] Static long-term user credentials if the target deployments require them.
- [ ] Decide whether supported coturn deployments need EVEN-PORT, reservation
  tokens, dual allocations, RFC 8489 SHA-256 auth or other extensions.
  Unsupported comprehension-required attributes currently receive 420.
- [x] Measure Linux receive batching and multiple independent processes before
  adding runtime paths; the development experiments retain their VM limits.
- [x] Measure a same-source M4 PGO trial; retain the ordinary release build
  because the small observed changes do not establish a useful gain.
- [ ] Repeat Linux performance and resource qualification on independent
  bare-metal hardware before generalising the virtual-machine observations.

TCP relay allocations (RFC 6062), DTLS client transport, database integrations,
OAuth, telnet/HTTP administration and clustering are outside the first release.
TURN over TCP/TLS still uses UDP sockets between the relay and its peers.
Do not silently remove transport support required by existing clients.

## Later integrations

- [ ] Archy operator-owned package, identity-independent transport credentials,
  deliberate opt-in exposure and resource limits. No default hosted service.
- [ ] Swift/Kotlin boundary and physical no-Play GrapheneOS acceptance if a
  native app needs to host a relay, separately from ordinary TURN client use.
- [ ] Assess Sapflow transport needs without adding codecs, SRT or HLS to the
  forwarding core, or claiming unmodified clients already speak TURN.

## Source: Changelog

Canonical source: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Extract owner-authorised pairing and scoped credentials into the reusable
  `spry-access` Rust library, with explicit calling-application configuration.
- Add `spry-service`, a reusable HTTP host adapter and standalone `spry-node`
  executable. Archipelago integration supplies its own UI/signing assets;
  standalone use requires no Archipelago installation.
- Keep forwarding in the independent `spry-turn` library and executable.
  Home-network mesh integration and physical-phone acceptance remain open.

## 0.2.1 — 23 October 2026

Public MIT prerelease. Stream readiness registrations now change only when
backpressure changes write interest. Public Rust configuration is unchanged.

- Native UDP/TCP/TLS benchmark tooling, loaded latency samples, explicit
  TLS verification, binary identities and live Linux socket-memory counters.
- Controlled M4 comparison against v0.2.0 and coturn, with TCP/TLS tuning
  gains, workload limits and memory trade-offs recorded.
- Twenty-seven socket tests, real backpressure transition coverage,
  sustained allocation churn, loss/jitter, expiry, slow-client recovery
  and coverage-guided ASan fuzzing. CI includes bounded stress and fuzz runs.
- Actual KithMoot web acceptance with relay credentials entered through
  device Settings, bidirectional generated media and no credential service.
  Public-network, physical GrapheneOS and Archy acceptance remain open.

## Public source, 23 October 2026

The owner authorised public MIT source and the existing GitHub prereleases.
History and release archives were checked before visibility changed. Existing
tags and archive bytes are retained; historical private-release wording below
describes their original creation. Package registries and hosted services remain
separate scope. This documentation change does not requalify runtime performance.

## 0.2.0 — 23 October 2026

Private prerelease. Adds a public `Config::relay_port_range` field; Rust
hosts using struct literals must supply it, or use `Config::local(secret)`.

- Optional inclusive `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST` bounds UDP peer allocations.
  Occupied ports are skipped; exhaustion returns 508 without falling back
  outside the range. Existing default ephemeral allocation is unchanged.
- Operator firewall/NAT/certificate plan and bounded-range socket/browser
  regression coverage. Public deployment qualification remains open.
- Versioned native/WASM release archives, current API/installation guides
  and regenerated LLM context. Donation destinations are unchanged.

## 0.1.0 — 23 October 2026

Initial private prerelease. No package registry, public relay or Archy
deployment is included. Full coturn parity and production qualification
remain open.

- Standalone Rust server and embeddable native library with STUN Binding,
  authenticated TURN UDP allocations, permissions, ChannelData and indications.
- UDP/TCP clients, optional rustls TLS, expiring shared-secret credentials
  and bounded allocation, connection and bandwidth resources.
- Borrowed forwarding buffers, generation-tagged readiness slots and the
  concrete-IPv4 connected-UDP optimisation, with socket trade-offs disclosed.
- Native ARM64 M4 Max comparison against coturn 4.18.0, with complete raw
  results and superseded translated-architecture runs identified.
- WASM packet arena and credential helpers, verified through actual execution.
- Independent UDP/TCP/TLS socket checks, relay-only generated browser media,
  Linux/macOS CI and explicit remaining qualification gates.
- Installation, integration, API, operations and coturn compatibility guides;
  ForgeSworn donation links and generated LLM navigation/full context checked
  for freshness in CI.

## Source: Contributing

Canonical source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Contributing

Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md). Keep the forwarding core
small, safe Rust and independent of media, application admission and hosted
services. Source and GitHub prereleases are public. Keep test fixtures
generated and free of private endpoints, credentials and media.

Use synthetic peers, credentials and media. Do not commit private endpoints,
real machine paths, keys or packet captures. Use this checkout's `target/`
and leave `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unchanged.

## Documentation

```sh
npm run docs:generate
npm run check:docs
```

These commands use Node 24 built-ins, without `npm install`. Edit source
guides rather than generated `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt`. The checker
validates generated context, local links, heading anchors and funding
destinations. See [maintaining documentation](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/maintaining-docs.md).

## Native checks

```sh
npm run check
cargo build --locked --release --features tls
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
python3 tests/stress.py --tls --seconds 180 --output .local/stress.json
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium
python3 tests/browser.py --tls
```

`npm run check` runs documentation validation, Rust formatting, clippy with
warnings denied, all-feature tests and both minimal library test sets.
The stress runner caps normal control traffic below admission limits and
tests a separate overload burst, expiry, churn and slow-client recovery.
Its seeded loss/jitter proxy is local qualification. A short soak and
coarse RSS samples do not prove absence of leaks or WAN acceptance.

Python orchestrates independent test sockets and browser fixtures; the
shipping server, library and socket load generator are Rust.

For coverage-guided ASan parser/auth fuzzing:

```sh
rustup toolchain install nightly-2025-12-05 --profile minimal
cargo install cargo-fuzz --version 0.13.2 --locked
python3 tests/fuzz.py --toolchain nightly-2025-12-05 --seconds 300 \
  --output .local/fuzz/receipt.json
```

The isolated [fuzz target](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/fuzz/README.md) has no effect on shipping
dependencies and reuses the checkout's `target/`. Its corpus and logs stay
under ignored `.local/fuzz/`. CI runs a bounded 30-second campaign; longer
manual runs are separate evidence. Test the actual KithMoot application with
the [operator acceptance runner](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md).

For WASM build and actual execution, use [the API commands](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md#wasm-build).
Run an appropriate credential/source scan before pushing; never suppress a
finding without inspecting and resolving its cause. Current CI runs native
checks and interop on Linux/macOS and builds the WASM codec on Linux.

## Performance and cleanup

Performance claims require matched executable architectures, real socket
workloads, alternating server order and disclosed resource costs. Use
[the current benchmark method](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/qualification-0.2.1.md); a framing microbenchmark
cannot establish network throughput. Preserve raw failure evidence alongside
successful runs and do not confuse loopback with production acceptance.

Stop task-owned servers and browsers and remove their fixtures. After a
safe merge, remove only build/scratch resources created by that task.
Preserve the explicitly named benchmark and verification evidence.

## Source: Coding-agent instructions

Canonical source: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/AGENTS.md)

# spry-turn

A small packet relay. Keep protocol adapters separate from forwarding and
resource limits. WebRTC, SRT, media codecs and media packaging are not runtime
dependencies. Transparent UDP is for an explicitly configured upstream;
TURN is optional. Do not silently turn either into an open arbitrary proxy.

- British English. MIT. Commit as TheCryptoDonkey with a GitHub no-reply email.
- The owner authorised public MIT source and the existing GitHub prereleases
  on 23 October 2026. Package registries, images, Pages and a hosted relay
  remain separate scope; do not add them without the owner's instruction.
- No real endpoints, credentials, private source, media or machine paths in
  committed evidence. Fixtures must be generated locally.
- `unsafe` is forbidden in our code. Keep dependency features small.
- Use this checkout's `target/`. Leave `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unchanged.
- Test outside-input parsing, authentication, permissions, state expiry and
  overload. Performance claims require reproducible socket measurements.
- Run fmt, clippy, tests, minimal-feature builds, interop and secret scanning.
- Stop task-owned servers and remove generated private fixtures afterwards.

## Source: Maintaining documentation

Canonical source: [docs/maintaining-docs.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/maintaining-docs.md)

# Maintaining documentation and discovery

Maintained source lives in the Markdown guides linked from
[the documentation index](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/README.md). `scripts/docs.mjs` owns the catalogue,
generates both LLM files and checks all tracked Markdown/TXT navigation.
The generator uses Node built-ins; it adds no server runtime dependency.

## Edit, generate, check

1. Update the relevant source guide and any changed examples or limitations.
2. Add a new primary guide to the catalogue in `scripts/docs.mjs` and the
   documentation index.
3. Run `npm run docs:generate`, then `npm run check:docs`.
4. Commit source and generated files together. CI rejects stale output,
   missing local files, broken local heading fragments and mismatched
   donation destinations.

`llms.txt` is a concise Markdown navigation file following
[the llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/). `llms-full.txt` bundles the
maintained guides using canonical absolute GitHub links. Both carry the
version and important implementation/qualification boundaries. Raw benchmark
JSON, dependency licence dumps, machine paths and ignored fixtures are not
bundled. Generated links use the canonical `forgesworn/spry-turn` repository.

The checker is deterministic and offline. It validates repository links
and fragments, not external site availability or GitHub rendering of a
Sponsor button. Recheck external donation pages when changing recipients.

## Repository metadata and privacy

Keep the GitHub description, repository topics, Cargo description, keywords
and documentation URL accurate. `publish = false` and npm's `private: true`
continue to block package publication. The public repository's root
`llms.txt` provides navigation for readers and tools.
There is no claim of search-engine ranking, model training inclusion or
guaranteed ingestion.

The owner authorised public MIT source and the existing GitHub prereleases
on 23 October 2026. Source history, fixtures and release artefacts were checked
for secrets and private paths before changing visibility; tags and archive
bytes were retained. A public Pages site, package registries and hosted relay
operation remain separate scope. Donation links are informational
and never grant transport or application access.

## Ship checklist

Run [the required checks](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), inspect the staged diff and
scan for secrets. Push a branch, merge its reviewed PR only after Linux/macOS
CI succeeds, then verify the merged head. Tag the reviewed commit and make
the GitHub release a prerelease while qualification remains incomplete. Verify the tag target, release
visibility and any downloaded asset checksums. Public packages, images,
Pages and a running TURN service require their own explicit scope.

Release builds must remap the builder's home-directory prefix before
packaging, so panic/source strings do not disclose private machine paths.
For example, supply `RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$HOME=/build"` to each
native and WASM release build. Scan the resulting binaries as well as
source. Include the MIT licence, dependency notices and a platform/scope
README in archives; publish SHA-256 checksums and a source-commit receipt.

## Source: Transport position

Canonical source: [docs/legal/transport-position.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/legal/transport-position.md)

# Packet transport position

Draft, 23 October 2026. Not legal advice; not reviewed by a lawyer. This is
a design position for the local implementation, not a deployment or
compliance assessment. The reviewed source is identified by file hashes in
the [source manifest](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/source-manifest.json).

The legal source is jurisdiction-kit's [GB online-services
note](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/law/gb/online-services.md),
verified overall on 28 September 2026 and due for review by 28 March 2027.
The local note includes partial primary-source checks dated 23 October
2026 for transport access facilities, public communications providers and
investigatory powers; those additions may precede the linked public copy.
`[P]` means primary text read in that note, not a settled application.
`[U]` means an unresolved interpretation or application to this design.

## Position today and intended operation

The owner has chosen software publication without a maintainer-operated
default relay or central KithMoot calling entitlement. The owner authorised
public MIT source and the existing GitHub prereleases on 23 October 2026.
Package-registry publication remains disabled in `Cargo.toml`.
The owner reports local implementation and tests only: no service is
deployed. Code publication, a build and a running communications service
are separate events. No public operational service is established by the
presence of server source.

The intended deployment is a standalone, coturn-style TURN server on an
independently operated Archy node. KithMoot would select it through ordinary
TURN configuration. Local KithMoot web interoperability is now qualified
with owner-selected credentials and no credential-service request; see the
[application receipt and limits](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/kithmoot-acceptance.md). Archy packaging,
actual operator independence, cross-network and physical-device acceptance
remain unproved. Sapflow support is a later optional goal.
Nothing here changes another application's deployment or legal position.

## Implemented boundary

The library's default listener is loopback; the executable requires an
operator-provided secret and explicit configuration to expose another
address (`src/turn.rs:186`, `src/main.rs:54`, `:82`). There is no runtime
hosted endpoint default or discovery lookup. The source has no application
room model, member directory, room-invitation authority or KithMoot
entitlement issuer. TURN resource authentication is separate from admission
to an application conversation. The REST credential
helper accepts an operator secret and a username, while server nonces bind
to address, time and realm (`src/auth.rs:13`, `:29`, `:54`, `:73`). An operator
that holds the secret can issue transport credentials; that fact does not give
it room membership authority (`src/turn.rs:937`).

Allocation, permission, channel and connection state is held in memory,
with expiry and capacity limits (`src/turn.rs:265`, `:433`, `:867`, `:1134`,
`:1170`, `:1358`, `:1369`). The forwarding paths relay datagrams between sockets
and keep aggregate packet/byte/drop counters (`src/turn.rs:977`, `:1427`,
`:1461`; `src/limits.rs:41`). The default optimisation can add a connected
client-facing UDP socket per authenticated UDP allocation for a concrete IPv4
listener on Unix, with a portable fallback (`Cargo.toml:17`, `:23`;
`src/turn.rs:477`, `:1172`). This retains the same transport credentials,
permissions and application-admission boundary. The reviewed code has no
payload-recording or per-client access-log writer. It emits startup/error diagnostics, and the
credential subcommand deliberately prints a credential pair
(`src/main.rs:36`, `:119`, `:152`). Host logs, shell history, process
inspection, crash handling and any service wrapper require a separate
deployment audit; in-memory expiry is not a forensic-erasure claim.

The relay handles network addresses, credential identifiers, permissions,
connection state and forwarded datagram bytes. It is not an end-to-end
media encryption implementation. Payload confidentiality depends on the
endpoints and application protocol. TLS terminates at the relay, which can
inspect the forwarded bytes after that link's protection is removed.
Use opaque transport-only credential labels: do not encode room identities
or personal identifiers merely for relay authentication.

## Legal reasoning and change boundary

The note's sections 1 and 2.2 distinguish software publication from service
operation. For the intended independent node, OSA section 226(12)'s
access-facility distinction exists `[P]` (note 2.11). Applying it to this
TURN deployment, separately from the underlying call service and its
admission authority, remains `[U]`. Replaceable, room-blind transport and
real independence support that distinction; encryption, a separate process
or a licence alone do not establish an exemption. Ordinary room invitations
are not automatically operation of the underlying service `[U]` (note 2.2).

A running node's metadata processing and any public forwarding need their
own conditional data-protection, communications and lawful-notice assessment
(note sections 3, 4.1, 5 and 7); this publisher position does not settle those
roles or promise immunity from legal process.

Before adopting the Archy deployment, confirm its actual operator,
credential control, independent substitution and separation from room
admission. Adding maintainer-run defaults, compulsory calling entitlements,
room control, discovery or media processing requires a fresh assessment.
Do not silently make ordinary client installations transit nodes. No
service-launch deadline or fee is assigned by this local publisher-only
assessment.

Not checked: non-UK law; actual Archy/KithMoot/Sapflow integration; live
infrastructure; real-device acceptance; or a complete public relay operator
assessment.
